signals.name: Age Verification Not Implemented
signals.description: No age verification mechanism exists for information society services offered directly to children. Article 8.1 requires reasonable efforts to verify age when relying on consent for processing children's data.
signals.applicability: Applicable to information society services offered directly to children under 16 (or lower age set by Member State). Controller must make reasonable efforts to verify that consent is given or authorized by holder of parental responsibility.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of services offered to children and absence of age verification or gating mechanisms.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter II - Conditions for Child Consent

signals.name: Parental Consent Not Obtained
signals.description: Parental consent has not been obtained or verified for processing personal data of children below the age of digital consent. Article 8.1 requires consent to be given or authorized by holder of parental responsibility for children.
signals.applicability: Applicable when processing children's data based on consent for information society services. Parent or guardian must provide or authorize consent for children below applicable age threshold.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of consent processes for child users and absence of parental consent collection or authorization mechanisms.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter II - Conditions for Child Consent

signals.name: Consent Not Freely Given
signals.description: Consent is not freely given due to conditioning of service on consent, clear imbalance between controller and data subject, or inability to refuse without detriment. Article 7.4 addresses conditioning of contracts on consent.
signals.applicability: Applicable when consent is used as legal basis. Consent must be freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous. Cannot condition service provision on consent for non-necessary processing.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of consent mechanisms, terms of service, and identification of consent bundling or conditioning practices.

signals.name: Consent Not Informed
signals.description: Consent is obtained without providing data subjects with adequate information about the processing. Article 7 requires informed consent, meaning data subjects must know identity of controller, purposes, and other Article 13/14 information.
signals.applicability: Applicable when obtaining consent for processing. Data subjects must receive all required transparency information before or at the time of consent to make informed decision.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of consent mechanisms and absence of required information at point of consent collection.

signals.name: Consent Records Not Maintained
signals.description: Controller does not maintain records demonstrating that valid consent was obtained. Article 7.1 requires controllers to be able to demonstrate that data subject has consented to processing.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all consent-based processing. Controller must maintain evidence of consent including who consented, when, what information was provided, and how consent was obtained.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of consent management systems and absence of consent records, timestamps, or audit trails.

signals.name: Consent Not Specific
signals.description: Consent is not specific to particular processing purposes or covers multiple purposes without granular options. Article 7 requires consent to be specific, and separate consent should be obtained for different processing operations.
signals.applicability: Applicable when seeking consent for processing activities. Each distinct processing purpose requires separate, specific consent. Blanket consent is not valid under GDPR.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of consent forms and identification of bundled purposes or vague consent requests without granular options.

signals.name: Consent Withdrawal Mechanism Missing
signals.description: No mechanism exists for data subjects to withdraw consent as easily as it was given. Article 7.3 requires that withdrawal be as easy as giving consent and that data subjects are informed of withdrawal right.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all consent-based processing. Withdrawal mechanism must be available, accessible, and as easy to use as initial consent mechanism. Processing must stop upon withdrawal.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of consent management systems and absence of clear, accessible withdrawal mechanisms.

signals.name: Compliance Measures Not Implemented
signals.description: The controller has not implemented appropriate technical and organizational measures to ensure and demonstrate GDPR compliance in accordance with Article 24.1. This includes failure to implement measures proportionate to processing risks and data volumes.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all data controllers processing personal data. Measures must be appropriate to the nature, scope, context, and purposes of processing as well as the risks to rights and freedoms of data subjects.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through assessment of organizational policies, technical controls, privacy documentation, and risk management frameworks. Requires evaluation of whether measures are appropriate and demonstrable.

signals.name: Data Return Process Not Established
signals.description: The processor contract does not provide for deletion or return of all personal data to the controller after the end of provision of services as required by Article 28.3(g). This includes failure to establish processes for secure data deletion and verification of deletion.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all processor relationships. Contracts must specify deletion or return procedures, exceptions for legal retention requirements, and verification mechanisms for data disposal.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of processor contracts, vendor termination procedures, and data return/deletion protocols. Requires verification that contractual provisions and operational procedures exist.

signals.name: EU Representative Not Designated
signals.description: A controller or processor not established in the EU but subject to GDPR has not designated a representative in the European Union as required by Article 27. The representative must be established in a Member State where data subjects whose data is processed are located.
signals.applicability: Applicable to controllers and processors not established in the EU whose processing activities are related to offering goods/services to EU data subjects or monitoring their behavior. Exceptions apply for occasional, non-systematic processing or public authorities.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of organizational establishment, processing scope targeting EU subjects, and documentation of EU representative designation. Requires verification of representative location and mandate.

signals.name: Joint Controller Arrangement Not Established
signals.description: Where two or more controllers jointly determine purposes and means of processing, no arrangement exists defining their respective responsibilities for GDPR compliance as required by Article 26. This includes failure to transparently communicate the arrangement to data subjects.
signals.applicability: Applicable when multiple entities jointly determine the purposes and means of processing personal data. Requires documented arrangements specifying compliance responsibilities and transparent communication to data subjects.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of partnership agreements, data sharing arrangements, and multi-party processing scenarios. Requires assessment of whether joint determination exists and if responsibilities are documented.

signals.name: Policy Documentation Not Maintained
signals.description: The controller has not adhered to approved codes of conduct or certification mechanisms, or lacks documented data protection policies as required by Article 24.2. This includes failure to maintain evidence of compliance measures and policy adherence.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all data controllers, particularly those using codes of conduct or certification as compliance mechanisms. Includes requirements for documented policies, procedures, and evidence of their implementation.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of policy documentation, certification records, code of conduct adherence, and compliance evidence. Requires verification that documented policies exist and are followed.

signals.name: Processing Instructions Not Documented
signals.description: The processor processes personal data without documented instructions from the controller or processes data beyond the scope of documented instructions as prohibited by Article 29. Processors must only process on documented instructions from the controller unless required by Union or Member State law.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all processor relationships. Controllers must provide clear, documented processing instructions and processors must adhere to them. Instructions should cover purposes, means, scope, and duration of processing.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of processor contracts, processing documentation, and operational procedures. Requires verification that instructions exist, are documented, and are followed by processors.

signals.name: Controller Processing Records Not Maintained
signals.description: The controller has not maintained records of processing activities under its responsibility as required by Article 30.1. Records must include controller and representative details, processing purposes, data subject and personal data categories, recipients, transfers, retention periods, and security measures.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all controllers except organizations with fewer than 250 employees unless processing is not occasional, likely to risk rights and freedoms, or includes special categories or criminal data. Records must be in writing and available to supervisory authorities.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of processing records, ROPA (Record of Processing Activities), data inventory, and compliance documentation. Requires verification that records are complete, current, and accessible.

signals.name: Processor Contract Not Established
signals.description: Processing by a processor is not governed by a contract or legal act binding the processor to the controller as required by Article 28.3. The contract must specify subject matter, duration, nature, purpose of processing, type of personal data, categories of data subjects, and controller/processor obligations.
signals.applicability: Applicable whenever a controller engages a processor to process personal data on its behalf. Requires written contracts or other legal acts containing mandatory clauses specified in Article 28.3.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of vendor contracts, service agreements, and processor relationships. Requires verification that contracts exist and contain all mandatory Article 28.3 clauses.

signals.name: Processor Due Diligence Not Performed
signals.description: The controller has not conducted due diligence to ensure the processor provides sufficient guarantees to implement appropriate technical and organizational measures as required by Article 28.1. This includes failure to assess processor capabilities before engagement.
signals.applicability: Applicable before engaging any processor and on an ongoing basis. Controllers must verify that processors can meet GDPR requirements and protect data subject rights.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of vendor selection processes, security assessments, compliance evaluations, and processor oversight procedures. Requires evidence of due diligence activities.

signals.name: Processor Processing Records Not Maintained
signals.description: The processor has not maintained records of all categories of processing activities carried out on behalf of controllers as required by Article 30.2. Records must include processor and representative details, categories of processing, transfers, and security measures.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all processors processing personal data on behalf of controllers, subject to same exceptions as controllers. Processors must maintain separate records for each controller and make them available to supervisory authorities.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of processor documentation, service records, and compliance with contractual record-keeping obligations. Requires verification that processors maintain adequate records for supervisory oversight.

signals.name: Sub-Processor Controls Not Implemented
signals.description: The processor has engaged sub-processors without prior authorization from the controller, or the controller lacks mechanisms to authorize and oversee sub-processors as required by Articles 28.2 and 28.4. This includes failure to impose equivalent data protection obligations on sub-processors.
signals.applicability: Applicable when processors engage other processors (sub-processors) to carry out processing activities. Requires controller authorization and contractual safeguards ensuring sub-processors meet GDPR obligations.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of processor contracts, sub-processor lists, authorization mechanisms, and downstream contractual requirements. Requires verification of authorization and equivalent obligations.

signals.name: Data Minimization Not Default
signals.description: Default system configurations do not limit the amount of personal data collected, the extent of processing, the period of storage, or accessibility as required by Article 25.2. Systems collect or retain more data than necessary for specified purposes without user action to enable such collection.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all data collection interfaces, storage systems, and processing operations. Default configurations must minimize data collection, processing scope, retention periods, and access.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through analysis of default data collection forms, storage configurations, retention policies, and access control defaults. Requires verification that minimal data collection is the default state.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter IV - Data Protection by Design and Default

signals.name: Privacy by Default Not Implemented
signals.description: The controller has not implemented data protection by default as required by Article 25.2. By default, systems process more personal data than necessary, make data accessible to more individuals than necessary, or retain data longer than necessary without individual intervention.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all processing operations and system configurations. Default settings must ensure that only personal data necessary for each specific purpose is processed by default.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of default system configurations, access permissions, data retention settings, and user consent flows. Requires verification that privacy-protective defaults are in place.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter IV - Data Protection by Design and Default

signals.name: Privacy by Design Not Implemented
signals.description: The controller has not implemented data protection by design as required by Article 25.1. Systems and processes lack appropriate technical and organizational measures such as pseudonymization integrated at the design stage to meet GDPR requirements and protect data subject rights.
signals.applicability: Applicable at the time of determining means of processing and at the time of processing itself. Covers system design, architecture decisions, software development, and infrastructure planning.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through architecture reviews, system design documentation, development practices, and evaluation of privacy controls integrated into systems. Requires assessment of whether privacy was considered from the outset.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter IV - Data Protection by Design and Default

signals.name: DPO Contact Details Not Published
signals.description: Contact details of the Data Protection Officer have not been published or communicated to the supervisory authority. Article 37.7 requires publication of DPO contact details and communication to the authority.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all organizations that have designated a DPO under Article 37. Contact details must be publicly available and communicated to the relevant supervisory authority.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of privacy notices, website publications, and supervisory authority notification records.

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Protection Officers

signals.name: DPO Not Designated
signals.description: Data Protection Officer has not been designated when required by Article 37.1. DPO designation is mandatory for public authorities, large-scale monitoring, or large-scale processing of special categories of data.
signals.applicability: Applicable to public authorities (except courts), organizations whose core activities require regular and systematic monitoring at large scale, or large-scale processing of special categories or criminal data.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through organizational assessment against DPO designation criteria and absence of designated DPO records.

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Protection Officers

signals.name: DPO Independence Not Ensured
signals.description: Data Protection Officer does not operate with sufficient independence or reports to management in a way that creates conflicts of interest. Article 38.3 requires DPOs to perform duties independently without instructions.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all DPO arrangements. DPO must not receive instructions regarding performance of tasks, must report to highest management level, and must not have conflicting duties.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of DPO reporting structure, job description, and potential conflicts of interest in dual roles.

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Protection Officers

signals.name: DPO Task Resources Not Provided
signals.description: Data Protection Officer has not been provided with necessary resources, support, or access to perform required tasks effectively. Article 38.2 requires controllers to support DPO in performing tasks.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all organizations with designated DPO. Controller must provide resources including staff, premises, equipment, and access to personal data and processing operations.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through assessment of DPO resources, budget allocation, staff support, and access to data and systems.

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Protection Officers

signals.name: DPIA Documentation Incomplete
signals.description: Data Protection Impact Assessment exists but does not contain required elements specified in Article 35.7, including systematic description of processing, necessity assessment, risk assessment, or mitigation measures.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all DPIAs conducted under Article 35. Documentation must include processing description, necessity and proportionality assessment, risk assessment, and safeguards.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of existing DPIA documentation for completeness against Article 35.7 requirements.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter IV - Data Protection Impact Assessment

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Protection Impact Assessment

signals.name: DPIA Process Not Established
signals.description: No Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) process exists for processing operations likely to result in high risk to rights and freedoms. Article 35.1 requires controllers to carry out DPIAs before processing.
signals.applicability: Applicable when processing operations are likely to result in high risk to rights and freedoms, including systematic evaluation, large-scale processing of special categories, or systematic monitoring of public areas.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of data protection governance framework and absence of DPIA procedures for high-risk processing activities.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter IV - Data Protection Impact Assessment

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Protection Impact Assessment

signals.name: DPIA Review Not Conducted
signals.description: Data Protection Impact Assessment is not reviewed when there is a change to the risk represented by processing operations. Article 35.11 requires controllers to assess whether processing is performed in accordance with the DPIA.
signals.applicability: Applicable when processing operations change materially, when risks evolve, or when new technologies are adopted that affect the original DPIA scope and conclusions.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through comparison of processing operations with original DPIA and absence of review records when changes occur.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter IV - Data Protection Impact Assessment

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Protection Impact Assessment

signals.name: Prior Consultation Not Conducted
signals.description: Controller has not consulted the supervisory authority prior to processing when DPIA indicates high risk that cannot be mitigated. Article 36 requires prior consultation when DPIA shows residual high risk.
signals.applicability: Applicable when DPIA indicates processing would result in high risk in absence of measures to mitigate the risk, and controller intends to proceed with processing.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of DPIAs with high residual risk and absence of supervisory authority consultation records.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter IV - Data Protection Impact Assessment

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Protection Impact Assessment

signals.name: Criminal Data Processing Without Authorization
signals.description: Personal data relating to criminal convictions and offences is processed without official authority or legal authorization. Article 10 restricts such processing to control by official authority or when authorized by law.
signals.applicability: Applicable to processing of criminal conviction and offence data. Includes background checks, employment screening, and any system storing criminal history information.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through data inventory review to identify criminal conviction data. Verify legal authorization or official authority basis for any such processing.

signals.name: Accountability Not Demonstrated
signals.description: The controller cannot demonstrate compliance with GDPR data protection principles. Accountability requires documented evidence of compliance measures and their effectiveness.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all data controllers. Includes documentation of policies, procedures, training records, impact assessments, and processing records.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of documentation, policies, and compliance evidence. Assess whether the controller can demonstrate compliance if requested by a supervisory authority.

signals.name: Data Accuracy Not Maintained
signals.description: Personal data is not kept accurate and up to date. Controllers must take reasonable steps to ensure inaccurate data is erased or rectified without delay.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all personal data storage and processing systems. Includes customer databases, HR systems, CRM platforms, and any system maintaining personal data records.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through data quality audits, duplicate detection, and review of data update processes. Assess whether mechanisms exist for data subjects to correct their data.

signals.name: Valid Consent Mechanism Missing
signals.description: When consent is the lawful basis for processing, no valid mechanism exists to obtain, record, or verify consent that meets GDPR requirements for being freely given, specific, informed, and unambiguous.
signals.applicability: Applicable where consent is used as the lawful basis for processing. Includes consent collection interfaces, preference centers, and consent management platforms.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of consent collection mechanisms, consent records, and user interfaces. Assess whether consent meets all GDPR validity requirements.

signals.name: Data Minimization Not Implemented
signals.description: More personal data is collected or retained than is necessary for the specified processing purposes. Data collection should be limited to what is adequate, relevant, and necessary.
signals.applicability: Applicable to data collection, storage, and retention decisions. Includes form fields, database schemas, data imports, and ongoing data retention practices.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of data collection forms, database schemas, and retention policies. Assess whether each data element is necessary for the stated purpose.

signals.name: Unfair Processing Practices
signals.description: Personal data is processed in ways that are detrimental, unexpected, or misleading to data subjects. Fair processing requires that data handling does not adversely affect individuals in ways they would not reasonably expect.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all personal data processing activities. Includes assessment of whether processing methods, outcomes, or uses could be considered unfair to data subjects.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of processing outcomes, data subject complaints, and impact assessments. Requires evaluation of whether processing could cause unjustified adverse effects.

signals.name: Integrity and Confidentiality Not Ensured
signals.description: Appropriate security measures are not implemented to protect personal data against unauthorized or unlawful processing, accidental loss, destruction, or damage.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all systems processing or storing personal data. Includes technical security controls, organizational measures, and physical security safeguards.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through security assessments, vulnerability scans, and review of security controls. Assess encryption, access controls, and incident response capabilities.

signals.name: Lawful Basis Not Documented
signals.description: The lawful basis for processing personal data is not documented for each processing activity. Controllers must identify and record the appropriate lawful basis before processing begins.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all personal data processing activities. Documentation should be maintained in records of processing activities as required by Article 30.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of records of processing activities and privacy documentation. Each processing activity should have an explicitly documented lawful basis.

signals.name: Processing Without Lawful Basis
signals.description: Personal data is processed without a valid lawful basis as defined in GDPR Article 6. Processing must be justified by consent, contract performance, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, or legitimate interests.
signals.applicability: Applicable to any processing of personal data. Includes data collection, storage, analysis, sharing, and any other operation performed on personal data.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of processing activities, privacy notices, and consent records. Requires mapping each processing activity to a documented lawful basis.

signals.name: Purpose Limitation Not Enforced
signals.description: Personal data is collected for specified purposes but processed for incompatible purposes without proper justification. Data must only be used for purposes that are compatible with the original collection purpose.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all personal data processing where data may be used for purposes beyond original collection. Includes data sharing, secondary analytics, and repurposing of collected data.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of records of processing activities, data flows, and purpose documentation. Compare stated collection purposes against actual processing activities.

signals.name: Storage Limitation Not Enforced
signals.description: Personal data is kept for longer than necessary for the purposes for which it was collected. Data should be retained only as long as needed and then securely deleted or anonymized.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all personal data storage systems. Includes databases, file systems, backups, archives, and any persistent storage of personal data.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of retention policies, data lifecycle management, and automated deletion mechanisms. Assess whether retention periods are defined and enforced.

signals.name: Lack of Processing Transparency
signals.description: Data subjects are not adequately informed about how their personal data is collected, used, or processed. Transparency requires clear, accessible, and comprehensive information about processing activities.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all personal data processing where data subjects should be informed. Includes direct and indirect data collection, and all subsequent processing activities.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of privacy notices, consent mechanisms, and data subject communications. Assess completeness, clarity, and accessibility of information provided.

signals.name: Special Category Data Not Protected
signals.description: Special category personal data (sensitive data) is processed without meeting the additional requirements of Article 9. This includes data revealing racial origin, political opinions, religious beliefs, health data, biometric data, and data concerning sex life or sexual orientation.
signals.applicability: Applicable to processing of special category data as defined in Article 9. Requires both a lawful basis under Article 6 and an exemption under Article 9.2.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through data classification review and processing activity assessment. Identify all special category data and verify appropriate exemptions and safeguards.

signals.name: Data Retention Periods Not Defined
signals.description: The organization has not established defined retention periods for personal data as required by GDPR Article 5(1)(e). This signal indicates that data may be kept longer than necessary for its original processing purpose, violating the storage limitation principle. Organizations must define and document specific retention periods for each category of personal data processed.
signals.applicability: Organizations processing personal data of EU residents, Data controllers and processors subject to GDPR, Organizations without documented data retention policies

metadata.detection_notes: Detection involves reviewing data retention policies, checking for documented retention schedules, and assessing whether retention periods are defined for all categories of personal data.

signals.name: Subject Access Request Mechanism Missing
signals.description: No mechanism exists for data subjects to obtain confirmation of whether their personal data is being processed and to access that data. The right of access is a fundamental data subject right.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all data controllers. Must provide mechanism for data subjects to request and receive copies of their personal data and processing information.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of data subject request handling capabilities. Verify ability to locate, compile, and provide all personal data for a given subject.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter III - Rights of the Data Subject

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Subject Rights

signals.name: Automated Decision-Making Not Disclosed
signals.description: Data subjects are not informed about the existence of automated decision-making including profiling, the logic involved, and the significance and envisaged consequences.
signals.applicability: Applicable when automated decision-making produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects data subjects. Includes profiling, algorithmic decisions, and AI-based processing.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of automated decision systems and associated disclosures. Verify meaningful information about logic and consequences is provided.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter III - Rights of the Data Subject

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Subject Rights

signals.name: Privacy Notice at Collection Missing
signals.description: When personal data is collected directly from data subjects, required information is not provided at the time of collection. Article 13 specifies mandatory information elements.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all direct data collection from data subjects. Includes online forms, registration processes, and any point where personal data is collected from individuals.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of data collection points and associated privacy notices. Verify all Article 13 required elements are provided at collection time.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter III - Rights of the Data Subject

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Subject Rights

signals.name: Data Copy Provision Not Implemented
signals.description: The controller cannot provide a copy of personal data undergoing processing in a commonly used electronic format when requested electronically.
signals.applicability: Applicable when access requests are made electronically. Data should be provided in a commonly used electronic format unless otherwise requested.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of data export capabilities and format options. Verify ability to provide structured, machine-readable copies of personal data.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter III - Rights of the Data Subject

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Subject Rights

signals.name: Data Erasure Mechanism Missing
signals.description: No mechanism exists to erase personal data without undue delay when erasure grounds apply. The right to erasure (right to be forgotten) must be technically implementable.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all personal data storage systems. Must enable complete erasure across all systems and backups where erasure grounds are met.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of data deletion capabilities and procedures. Verify ability to completely remove personal data from all systems.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter III - Rights of the Data Subject

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Subject Rights

signals.name: Erasure Not Propagated to Recipients
signals.description: When personal data has been made public or disclosed to recipients, erasure requests are not communicated to those recipients. Controllers must take reasonable steps to inform processors of erasure.
signals.applicability: Applicable when personal data has been shared with third parties or made publicly available. Includes data sharing partners and search engines for public data.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of data sharing relationships and erasure notification procedures. Verify mechanisms to notify all recipients of erasure requests.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter III - Rights of the Data Subject

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Subject Rights

signals.name: Human Intervention Mechanism Missing
signals.description: No mechanism exists for data subjects to obtain human intervention, express their point of view, or contest automated decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects.
signals.applicability: Applicable when automated decision-making is permitted under Article 22.2 exceptions. Safeguards must include human intervention capability.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of automated decision systems and appeal/review mechanisms. Verify human review process exists and is accessible.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter III - Rights of the Data Subject

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Subject Rights

signals.name: Identity Verification Not Implemented
signals.description: No mechanism exists to verify the identity of data subjects making rights requests when reasonable doubts exist. Verification must balance security with accessibility of rights.
signals.applicability: Applicable to data subject rights request handling where identity verification is needed. Must not create unnecessary barriers to exercising rights.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of identity verification procedures for rights requests. Assess whether verification is proportionate and does not unduly burden data subjects.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter III - Rights of the Data Subject

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Subject Rights

signals.name: Indirect Collection Notice Missing
signals.description: When personal data is obtained from sources other than the data subject, required information is not provided within a reasonable period. Article 14 specifies mandatory information and timing requirements.
signals.applicability: Applicable when personal data is obtained from third parties, public sources, or other indirect means. Notice must be provided within one month or at first communication.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of data sources and associated notification processes. Verify Article 14 requirements are met for all indirect data collection.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter III - Rights of the Data Subject

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Subject Rights

signals.name: Direct Marketing Opt-Out Missing
signals.description: No mechanism exists for data subjects to object to processing for direct marketing purposes. This right is unconditional and must be presented clearly at first communication.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all direct marketing activities. The right to object to marketing is absolute and requires easy-to-use opt-out mechanisms.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of marketing communications and opt-out mechanisms. Verify unsubscribe links, preference centers, and marketing suppression processes.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter III - Rights of the Data Subject

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Subject Rights

signals.name: Objection Mechanism Missing
signals.description: No mechanism exists for data subjects to object to processing based on legitimate interests or public task grounds. Controllers must cease processing unless compelling legitimate grounds exist.
signals.applicability: Applicable when processing is based on legitimate interests (Art. 6.1.f) or public task (Art. 6.1.e). Must enable objection handling and assessment.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of objection handling procedures and processing controls. Verify ability to receive, assess, and act on objections.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter III - Rights of the Data Subject

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Subject Rights

signals.name: Data Portability Mechanism Missing
signals.description: No mechanism exists to provide personal data in a structured, commonly used, machine-readable format or to transmit data directly to another controller when technically feasible.
signals.applicability: Applicable when processing is based on consent or contract and carried out by automated means. Enables data subjects to obtain and reuse their data.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of data export capabilities and interoperability features. Verify structured export formats and controller-to-controller transfer options.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter III - Rights of the Data Subject

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Subject Rights

signals.name: Privacy Policy Not Accessible
signals.description: A comprehensive privacy policy is not accessible to data subjects. The policy should consolidate all required transparency information in an easily accessible location.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all organizations processing personal data. The privacy policy should be prominently linked and available across all data collection touchpoints.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of website and application for privacy policy presence and accessibility. Verify policy is findable, current, and complete.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter III - Rights of the Data Subject

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Subject Rights

signals.name: Recipient Notification Not Implemented
signals.description: Recipients to whom personal data has been disclosed are not notified of rectification, erasure, or restriction of processing as required by Article 19.
signals.applicability: Applicable when personal data has been shared with recipients. Controllers must notify recipients of changes unless impossible or disproportionate.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of data sharing records and notification procedures. Verify tracking of recipients and communication mechanisms.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter III - Rights of the Data Subject

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Subject Rights

signals.name: Data Rectification Mechanism Missing
signals.description: No mechanism exists for data subjects to obtain rectification of inaccurate personal data or completion of incomplete data without undue delay.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all personal data storage systems. Must enable correction of inaccuracies and completion of incomplete records upon request.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of data correction procedures and self-service capabilities. Verify ability to update personal data across all systems.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter III - Rights of the Data Subject

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Subject Rights

signals.name: Data Subject Request Response Missing
signals.description: No mechanism exists to respond to data subject requests without undue delay and within the required one-month timeframe. Controllers must be able to receive, process, and respond to rights requests.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all data subject rights request handling. Includes access requests, erasure requests, and all other rights under Articles 15-22.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of request handling procedures, response tracking systems, and historical response times. Verify ability to meet one-month deadline.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter III - Rights of the Data Subject

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Subject Rights

signals.name: Processing Restriction Mechanism Missing
signals.description: No mechanism exists to restrict processing of personal data when applicable conditions are met, such as during accuracy verification or when processing is contested.
signals.applicability: Applicable when data subjects request restriction under Article 18 conditions. Must be able to limit processing while retaining data.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of data processing controls and restriction capabilities. Verify ability to flag and limit processing of specific data records.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter III - Rights of the Data Subject

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Subject Rights

signals.name: Transparent Communication Not Provided
signals.description: Information about data processing is not provided in a concise, transparent, intelligible, and easily accessible form using clear and plain language, particularly when addressing children.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all communications with data subjects about processing activities. Includes privacy notices, consent forms, and responses to data subject requests.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of privacy communications for clarity, accessibility, and language. Assess readability level and presentation format.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter III - Rights of the Data Subject

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Data Subject Rights

signals.name: Access Control Not Implemented
signals.description: Systems lack appropriate access control measures to ensure that only authorized personnel can access personal data. Access control includes authentication, authorization, least privilege, separation of duties, and access monitoring.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all systems storing or processing personal data. Includes user authentication systems, database access, API endpoints, administrative interfaces, file storage, and processor access to controller data.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through access control configuration review and code analysis. Look for missing authentication, weak passwords, shared credentials, overly permissive roles, lack of MFA, no access logs, missing authorization checks, default credentials, and inadequate access provisioning/deprovisioning processes. Verify processor personnel access is documented and authorized.

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Security of Processing

signals.name: Availability Measures Not Implemented
signals.description: Systems lack adequate measures to ensure ongoing availability of personal data processing systems. Availability ensures that data and processing capabilities remain accessible to authorized users when needed, supporting data subject rights and business operations.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all systems processing personal data, particularly those supporting data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure). Includes redundancy, monitoring, incident response, and service continuity measures.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through infrastructure and architecture review. Look for single points of failure, lack of redundancy or failover mechanisms, missing health monitoring, no uptime SLAs, inadequate capacity planning, missing load balancing, and no disaster recovery testing. Assess whether system downtime impacts data subject rights.

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Security of Processing

signals.name: Breach Detection Mechanisms Not Implemented
signals.description: Organization lacks mechanisms to detect personal data breaches in a timely manner. Breach detection capabilities are essential to meet the 72-hour notification requirement and minimize harm to data subjects.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all systems processing personal data. Includes security monitoring, intrusion detection, anomaly detection, audit log analysis, incident alerting, and security information and event management (SIEM) systems.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through security operations review. Look for missing security monitoring, no intrusion detection system (IDS), lack of log aggregation, no anomaly detection, missing alerting mechanisms, inadequate audit trails, no SIEM solution, and absence of security incident response procedures. Verify monitoring covers all systems processing personal data.

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Security of Processing

signals.name: Breach Documentation Not Maintained
signals.description: Organization does not document all personal data breaches, including their facts, effects, and remedial actions. Controllers must maintain comprehensive records of all breaches regardless of whether supervisory authority notification was required.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all controllers. Documentation must cover all breaches, including those not requiring notification. Records must include breach facts, effects on data subjects, remedial actions taken, and justification if notification was not required.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through documentation review and incident records audit. Look for missing breach register, incomplete incident records, no documentation of remedial actions, missing risk assessments, absence of notification decisions, and lack of breach analysis. Verify documentation enables supervisory authority verification of GDPR compliance.

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Security of Processing

signals.name: Breach Notification Process Not Established
signals.description: Organization lacks a documented process for notifying supervisory authorities of personal data breaches within 72 hours. A breach notification process must include incident assessment, notification procedures, contact information, and decision workflows.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all controllers and processors. Controllers must notify supervisory authority within 72 hours unless breach is unlikely to result in risk. Processors must notify controllers without undue delay. Process must cover breach assessment, notification content, escalation, and timing.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through incident response plan review. Look for missing breach notification procedures, no supervisory authority contact information, undefined notification timelines, lack of breach assessment criteria, no notification templates, unclear roles and responsibilities, and absence of processor notification obligations in contracts. Verify process includes 72-hour deadline tracking.

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Security of Processing

signals.name: Confidentiality Measures Not Implemented
signals.description: Systems lack adequate measures to ensure ongoing confidentiality of personal data. Confidentiality ensures that data is accessible only to authorized individuals, systems, and processes.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all systems processing personal data. Includes access controls, authentication mechanisms, network segmentation, data classification, and employee training on confidentiality obligations.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through security audits, access control reviews, and code analysis. Look for missing authentication, weak authorization checks, overly permissive access rights, lack of role-based access control (RBAC), exposed APIs without authentication, and shared credentials. Review logging of data access events.

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Security of Processing

signals.name: Encryption Not Implemented
signals.description: Personal data is not encrypted in transit or at rest where appropriate, exposing data to unauthorized access. Encryption protects data confidentiality by rendering it unreadable without proper decryption keys.
signals.applicability: Applicable to systems transmitting or storing personal data, particularly sensitive personal data or data processed at scale. Includes databases, backups, API communications, and file storage systems.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through infrastructure review, code analysis, and network traffic inspection. Check for unencrypted database connections, HTTP instead of HTTPS, unencrypted storage volumes, plaintext backups, and missing TLS/SSL configurations. Review encryption key management practices.

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Security of Processing

signals.name: Integrity Measures Not Implemented
signals.description: Systems lack adequate measures to ensure ongoing integrity of personal data. Integrity ensures that data remains accurate, complete, and unaltered except by authorized processes, protecting against unauthorized modification or corruption.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all systems storing or processing personal data. Includes data validation, checksums, audit trails, version control, input sanitization, and protection against tampering or corruption.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through code review and architecture analysis. Look for missing input validation, lack of checksums or hashing for data verification, no audit logs for data modifications, missing database constraints, absence of data integrity checks, and inadequate protection against SQL injection or data corruption.

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Security of Processing

signals.name: Pseudonymization Not Implemented
signals.description: Personal data is not pseudonymized where appropriate, increasing risk in case of unauthorized access or breach. Pseudonymization renders data less identifiable while allowing processing for legitimate purposes.
signals.applicability: Applicable to systems processing personal data where pseudonymization is technically feasible and appropriate given the nature, scope, context, and purposes of processing. Particularly relevant for analytics, research, and systems with elevated breach risk.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through code review of data processing pipelines, database schemas, and data transformation logic. Look for direct storage of identifiers (names, emails, IDs) without tokenization or hashing. Review data minimization practices and whether direct identifiers are necessary for processing purposes.

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Security of Processing

signals.name: Recovery Capability Not Implemented
signals.description: Systems lack the ability to restore availability and access to personal data in a timely manner after a physical or technical incident. Recovery capability includes backup procedures, disaster recovery plans, and tested restoration processes.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all systems storing or processing personal data. Includes regular backups, offsite storage, documented recovery procedures, recovery time objectives (RTO), recovery point objectives (RPO), and tested recovery processes.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through backup and disaster recovery plan reviews. Look for missing backup schedules, no offsite backups, untested recovery procedures, undefined RTO/RPO, lack of backup verification, missing recovery documentation, and no disaster recovery drills. Review whether backups include all personal data systems.

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Security of Processing

signals.name: Resilience Measures Not Implemented
signals.description: Systems lack resilience to withstand and recover from incidents affecting personal data processing. Resilience encompasses the ability to maintain operations during disruptions, adapt to changing conditions, and recover quickly from failures or attacks.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all systems processing personal data. Includes fault tolerance, graceful degradation, incident response capabilities, backup systems, and ability to operate under adverse conditions such as attacks or infrastructure failures.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through architecture review and disaster recovery testing. Look for lack of error handling, no graceful degradation, missing circuit breakers, single points of failure, no incident response plan, inadequate redundancy, and absence of chaos engineering or resilience testing. Review ability to operate during DDoS attacks or system failures.

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Security of Processing

signals.name: Security Risk Assessment Not Performed
signals.description: Organization has not assessed the risks to data subject rights and freedoms when determining appropriate security measures. Risk assessment should consider likelihood and severity of risks, the nature of personal data, and the state of the art in security technology.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all personal data processing activities. Risk assessment must consider nature, scope, context, and purposes of processing, and guide selection of appropriate technical and organizational security measures proportionate to the identified risks.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through documentation review and governance assessment. Look for missing risk assessment documentation, no threat modeling, undefined risk appetite, lack of documented security controls mapping to risks, no consideration of data sensitivity levels, and absence of risk treatment plans. Verify risk assessments are updated when processing changes.

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Security of Processing

signals.name: Security Testing Not Implemented
signals.description: Organization lacks a process for regularly testing, assessing, and evaluating the effectiveness of technical and organizational security measures. Regular security testing is essential to identify vulnerabilities and ensure ongoing protection of personal data.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all personal data processing systems and security controls. Includes penetration testing, vulnerability scanning, security audits, code reviews, disaster recovery testing, and ongoing security assessments.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through security program review and documentation analysis. Look for absence of security testing schedule, no penetration testing reports, missing vulnerability scans, no security audit trail, lack of code security reviews, untested incident response plans, and no evidence of security assessments. Review whether findings from testing are tracked and remediated.

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Security of Processing

signals.name: Data Subject Breach Notification Process Not Established
signals.canonical_name: Data Subject Breach Notification Process Not Established
signals.description: Organization lacks a process for notifying data subjects of personal data breaches when the breach is likely to result in a high risk to their rights and freedoms. Data subject notification must be clear, direct, and timely when high risk is identified.
signals.applicability: Applicable to controllers when a breach is likely to result in high risk to data subjects. Process must include high-risk assessment criteria, notification content requirements, communication methods, timing, and exceptions where notification can be avoided through protective measures.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through incident response documentation review. Look for missing data subject notification procedures, no high-risk assessment criteria, lack of notification templates, undefined communication channels, no process for mass notification, missing exceptions documentation, and absence of notification tracking. Verify process considers encryption and other protective measures that may eliminate notification requirement.

sources.title: EDPB Guidelines on Security of Processing

signals.name: Adequacy Decision Not Verified
signals.description: Transfer to third country relies on adequacy decision but verification of current adequacy status has not been performed. Article 45 allows transfers based on Commission adequacy decisions.
signals.applicability: Applicable when relying on European Commission adequacy decisions for data transfers. Must verify country/territory has valid adequacy decision and monitor for changes or invalidations.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of transfer mechanisms and absence of adequacy decision verification or monitoring processes.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter V - Transfers to Third Countries

signals.name: Binding Corporate Rules Not Approved
signals.description: Multinational organization relies on Binding Corporate Rules (BCRs) for intra-group transfers but BCRs have not been approved by competent supervisory authority. Article 47 requires BCR approval.
signals.applicability: Applicable to multinational groups transferring data between entities in different countries. BCRs must be approved by lead supervisory authority and meet Article 47 requirements.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of intra-group transfer mechanisms and absence of approved BCR documentation or supervisory authority approval.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter V - Transfers to Third Countries

signals.name: Derogation Not Documented
signals.description: Transfer to third country relies on Article 49 derogation but specific situation and necessity are not documented. Derogations are limited to specific situations and must be documented with justification.
signals.applicability: Applicable when transfers occur without adequacy or safeguards, relying on derogations. Must be occasional, necessary, and documented. Not available for systematic or large-scale transfers.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of transfers without adequacy or safeguards and absence of derogation justification documentation.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter V - Transfers to Third Countries

signals.name: Appropriate Safeguards Not Implemented
signals.description: Transfer to third country without adequacy decision lacks appropriate safeguards as required by Article 46. Safeguards include binding corporate rules, standard contractual clauses, or approved codes of conduct.
signals.applicability: Applicable to transfers to third countries without adequacy decision. Controller or processor must provide appropriate safeguards and ensure enforceable data subject rights.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of contracts with third country processors and absence of appropriate safeguards mechanisms.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter V - Transfers to Third Countries

signals.name: Standard Contractual Clauses Not Used
signals.description: Transfer to third country processor or controller does not utilize European Commission approved Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs). Article 46.2.c allows transfers based on SCCs adopted by the Commission.
signals.applicability: Applicable when transferring data to third countries without adequacy decision and relying on contractual safeguards. SCCs must be Commission-approved and not modified.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through contract review with third country vendors and absence of valid SCCs or use of outdated SCC versions.

sources.title: GDPR - Regulation (EU) 2016/679
sources.section: Chapter V - Transfers to Third Countries

signals.name: Transfer Assessment Not Conducted
signals.description: No assessment has been conducted to determine whether personal data transfers to third countries or international organizations comply with GDPR requirements. Article 44 establishes general principles for transfers.
signals.applicability: Applicable to all transfers of personal data to third countries or international organizations, regardless of processing location or transfer mechanism.

metadata.detection_notes: Detected through review of data flows, vendor locations, and absence of transfer impact assessments or legal basis documentation.
